citations.narrative:
Two parakeets died due to trauma. On 5/17/2026, parakeet #76207 sustained severe injuries when an employee
inadvertently caught the bird under an aviary door. The injury was not noticed immediately. Once discovered, the bird was
taken to the veterinary clinic, where it was determined the injuries were irreparable, and the bird was euthanized. On
7/14/2026, parakeet #76680 was accidentally stepped on and killed by a member of the public in the interactive parakeet
exhibit. The usual protocol for public interaction is to have members of the public sit on benches to control movement
while the birds are on the floor. The benches had been removed for maintenance, so patrons were standing while the
attendant cleared birds from the floor. A patron began moving before the attendant finished and accidentally stepped on a
bird.
Improper handling can result in injury or death and negatively affect animal welfare. Handling of all animals shall be done
as expeditiously and carefully as possible in a manner that does not cause trauma, overheating, excessive cooling,
behavioral stress, physical harm, or unnecessary discomfort.
These issues were corrected prior to the 7/16/2026 inspection by installing a window at the bottom of the door and adding
cement to prevent the door from swinging too far. Additionally, benches were placed back in the aviary to reduce standing
foot traffic.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
